Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
- New severe left-sided headache since early morning, woke patient from sleep; ongoing. Mild photophobia; paracetamol ineffective. No fever, neck stiffness, nausea/vomiting, or focal neurologic deficits. Ultimately improves when lying down. Work stress and sleep disruption present.
- Most consistent with migraine without aura (DDx supports high likelihood) versus tension-type headache (moderate likelihood given stress history but less consistent with unilateral severe pain and photophobia). Cluster headache less likely (no autonomic features; improves with lying down).
- Red flags considered: awoke from sleep noted; currently low concern for intracranial hemorrhage, mass, venous thrombosis, or dissection given absence of focal deficits, progressive symptoms, fever/neck stiffness, or typical risk factors (DDx alignment). Safety-net provided.
- Mental health: Established anxiety on sertraline; no current high-risk features; counseling resources discussed.

Management Plan
- Start ibuprofen as first-line for suspected migraine (dose/route/frequency not documented). May continue paracetamol if desired.
- Non-pharmacologic: Hydration goal 1.5–2.0 L/day (excluding caffeinated drinks). Sleep hygiene aiming for 7–8 hours/night. Stress reduction; consider self-certifying up to 1 week off work.
- Counseling: Provided information/link for local counseling service for stress management (self-referral).
- Follow-up: GP review in 1 week; earlier if worsening or new red-flag symptoms.
- Safety-net: Provided written information on danger signs of headaches; advised to seek care promptly if symptoms escalate.
- Future considerations: If not improving, consider blood tests and further evaluation.

- Migraine without aura — High likelihood: Acute unilateral severe headache with mild photophobia; stress/sleep disruption; paracetamol ineffective; improves with rest.
- Tension-type headache — Moderate likelihood: History of stress-related frontal headaches; current features (unilateral, photophobia, severity) are less typical.
- Cluster headache — Low–Moderate likelihood: Unilateral and awakened from sleep, but lacks autonomic features and improves when lying down.
